## Purpose and Entry Points
OpenHarness is a Python agent harness for LLM-driven coding and automation: provider access, iterative tool use, memory, permissions, extensions, and multi-agent work. Its primary CLI entry points are `src/openharness/__main__.py` and `src/openharness/cli.py`. `ohmo` is a personal-agent application layered over this harness, entered through `ohmo/__main__.py` and `ohmo/cli.py`, with chat-channel gateway support.

## Runtime Assembly and UI Boundary
The UI/runtime layer builds and owns interactive sessions, selecting either a React terminal frontend or Textual-based interface. The Python backend exposes a protocol/session host to the TypeScript terminal client, separating model/tool execution from rendering and input handling.
- `src/openharness/ui/runtime.py`
- `src/openharness/ui/backend_host.py`
- `frontend/terminal/src/App.tsx`

Headless CLI operation supports text, JSON, and stream-JSON outputs, using the same underlying runtime rather than a separate automation engine.

## Model Provider and Authentication Layer
Provider abstraction normalizes Anthropic-compatible, OpenAI-compatible, Codex, Copilot, and subscription-backed clients behind a registry/client boundary. Auth flows and persistent credential storage are separate from request execution, allowing named provider profiles and switching without changing agent-loop code.
- `src/openharness/api/registry.py`
- `src/openharness/api/client.py`
- `src/openharness/auth/manager.py`

External dependencies include remote LLM APIs, local Claude/Codex credential files, and GitHub Copilot OAuth. Compatible endpoints can include hosted providers or local Ollama.

## Agent Execution Loop
`QueryEngine` is the central control loop: it assembles messages and tool schemas, streams model responses, detects tool-use turns, executes calls, appends results, and repeats until completion. It also owns message/event handling and cost tracking boundaries.
- `src/openharness/engine/query_engine.py`
- `src/openharness/engine/query.py`
- `src/openharness/engine/stream_events.py`

The critical flow is: prompt/session context → provider stream → requested tool calls → guarded execution/results → next model turn. Streaming events feed both terminal UI and machine-readable output modes.

## Tool, Safety, and Extension Boundary
Tools implement the agent’s side effects: filesystem, shell, web, MCP, tasks, teams, scheduling, and user interaction. Permission checking gates execution, while lifecycle hooks can inspect or modify pre/post-tool behavior. This is the primary trust boundary for writes, commands, network access, and project-provided extensions.
- `src/openharness/tools/base.py`
- `src/openharness/permissions/checker.py`
- `src/openharness/hooks/executor.py`

Skills, plugins, slash commands, and output styles are loaded dynamically and contribute instructions, commands, hooks, agents, and MCP configuration without modifying the core engine.
- `src/openharness/skills/loader.py`
- `src/openharness/plugins/loader.py`
- `src/openharness/commands/registry.py`

## Context, Persistence, and MCP
Prompt construction combines system instructions, environment/project context, discovered `CLAUDE.md` content, skills, and memory. Session storage supports resume/history; memory services maintain persistent and relevance-selected knowledge across sessions. MCP is an external-tool boundary supporting stdio and HTTP servers, resource reads, authentication, reconnect behavior, and schema-derived tools.
- `src/openharness/prompts/system_prompt.py`
- `src/openharness/memory/manager.py`
- `src/openharness/mcp/client.py`

## Coordination and ohmo Gateway
OpenHarness can delegate work to in-process or subprocess agents, organize teams, synchronize permissions, manage mailboxes, and isolate work through git worktrees. `ohmo` converts channel messages into harness sessions through a gateway/router, then sends resulting responses and notifications back to configured chat platforms.
- `src/openharness/swarm/team_lifecycle.py`
- `src/openharness/swarm/subprocess_backend.py`
- `ohmo/gateway/router.py`

Channel adapters include Telegram, Slack, Discord, Feishu, email, WhatsApp, Matrix, and others; the channel bus decouples inbound events from gateway processing.
- `src/openharness/channels/adapter.py`
- `src/openharness/channels/bus/queue.py`
- `ohmo/gateway/service.py`
